C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION.Summary: Give one backend search-session coordinator ownership of event ordering and finalization across every validated root and both engines, so multi-root search delivers all roots' results before exactly one session terminal.
C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION.Problem: Confirmed against the current read-only state of the canary-beta-wave tree and by the SHA256-bound historical diagnostics from review checkout main 0a72917c. In src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs the mt_search_spawn worker thread iterates all validated_roots; the embedded walker run_search emits its own per-root terminal "complete"/"cancelled" event and restarts seq per root, and the outer thread then emits a second session terminal. For two roots the producer trace is match, complete, match, complete, complete with seq 1,2,1,2,1. The renderer consumer in src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/search.ts settles its thenable, unsubscribes and stops collecting on the first terminal event, so the second root's matches are lost whenever the embedded engine runs (App Store builds and desktop builds without rg); the rg control path returns both roots. Existing diagnostics (eight backend, eight frontend cases) prove the problem but do not establish native transport or App Store acceptance.
C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION.Relationship: Child finding of the original record COMPLEX:F-005; the duplicated completion ownership and the lost second-root results are the open items of its search group. Independent of C-SEARCH-INPUT-COMPOSITION-CONTRACT (exclusion-glob validation and size ingress), which currently lives only in the separate search-input-composition worktree and is not part of this tree; the future plan must rebase this change onto the actual delivery baseline it selects. Builds on the F-SEARCH-RIPGREP-SHELLOUT and C-15 engine-selection decisions without changing them. Delivered through the repository technical-debt lane; lane departure into main and train accounting are separate owner-controlled steps.

Goals.Goal: A successfully started search over multiple authorized roots delivers every matching root's results before one final complete event, with the same session semantics for the embedded walker and the rg execution.

One production session owner allocates strictly increasing seq values across all emitted match and terminal events. Root-level engines do not independently finalize the session or reset its event sequence.

A returned engine error ends the session with one error event and no later complete or matches. An observed cancellation ends it with one cancelled event; successful exhaustion of all roots ends it with complete. Terminal finalization cannot occur twice.

Preserve the existing renderer thenable/cancel contract, per-search filtering, stale-generation protection and unsubscribe behavior without a renderer workaround that waits through premature backend terminals.
Keep cancellation registration, rg child cleanup and registry removal correct for success, returned errors and requested cancellation, including cancellation between roots.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep the existing command names (mt_search_spawn, mt_search_cancel), the mt::search-event channel, searchId, kind values, hits/error payload fields and wire types. Do not add a root-count handshake, new terminal kind, event channel or frontend completion heuristic.

Use a bounded internal ownership correction in M-004. Existing engine helpers may be adapted or wrapped, but all production roots must pass through the same session finalization path; test-only duplicated coordinators cannot establish correctness.

Retain root validation and sandbox authorization before spawning work (M-010 check_path per root), engine selection for App Store builds and missing-rg fallback, current search options, batch/line bounds, result payload formatting and ordinary root traversal order.

Validation failures before a worker starts remain invoke failures rather than successful started streams. Unknown or already finished cancellation remains harmless and cannot publish a second terminal or revive a session.

Respect existing failure detection and renderer-observable fail-fast errors. This change does not redesign rg exit-status interpretation, file-read skipping or error classification. Already returned engine errors must not be followed by further root work or a success terminal.
Preserve existing cancellation timing budgets, source guards, retries, skips and coverage floors. Do not increase startup delays, timeouts or retries to hide event-order failures.
Keep query text, match contents and user paths out of any new diagnostic fields; use the existing semantic contracts and synchronize M-004/V-M-004 plus relevant bridge verification when implementing.

ObservedWriteScope (exact, verified present in the current tree): src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs (session coordinator and its inline #[cfg(test)] tests); tests/renderer/node/ripgrepSearcher-deep.test.js; tests/renderer/ipc/runtime-search.test.ts; tests/renderer/store/search.test.ts; .grace/graph/runtime.xml (M-004 module map and file-local contracts); .grace/verification/runtime.xml (V-M-004 and related bridge entries). No production renderer file is modified: src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/search.ts, src/renderer/src/store/search.js and src/renderer/src/node/ripgrepSearcher.js keep their current behavior and remain read-only anchors for wire compatibility.

Baseline divergence: the search-input-composition worktree (C-SEARCH-INPUT-COMPOSITION-CONTRACT, dated 2026-11-16) carries exclusion-glob implementation in its src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs, exclusions/maxFileSize pass-through in its typed IPC, and two additional ingress tests (tests/renderer/search-size-ingress.test.ts, tests/renderer/search-exclusions-ingress.test.ts) that are absent from the current tree. This change neither depends on nor absorbs that work; the plan must identify the actual lane baseline and, if composition changes are included, keep both scopes separate and rerun the composition regressions on that baseline.

The ownership correction is delivered through the repository's technical-debt lane. The future plan must bind to the actual prepared delivery baseline and required checks; this draft inspection tree is context only. Lane departure into main needs its separate owner instruction.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No maxFileSize conversion, inclusion/exclusion implementation, context-line support, UTF-8 truncation fix, rg exit-status repair, search ranking, streaming-performance redesign or cancellation-deadline redesign. Separate original records and additional observations stay open, including the composition track's scope.

No change to document saves, preferences storage, workspace root ownership, signing-boundary C-50, dependency acquisition, release version, tag, signing, workflow dispatch, installation or publication.
No assertion that controlled event replay proves native Tauri ordering, App Store platform acceptance or owner acceptance. No general worker framework or unrelated module split.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first tests execute the same production session coordinator used by mt_search_spawn. One-root and two-root success, zero matches and batched results have exactly one complete after all matches, strictly increasing seq and no event after the terminal, for both engine adapters.

The two-root embedded regression returns both synthetic files through the actual shim and full renderer searcher. It settles and unsubscribes once after the last root's results, with the same observable behavior as the rg control. A test that truncates capture at the first terminal is insufficient to prove the complete producer trace.

Pre-start cancellation, cancellation during a root, cancellation between roots, repeated cancellation and cancellation after completion do not produce duplicate terminal events or later matches. Returned engine errors are tested for both adapters; the remaining roots are not started, the renderer rejects once and no complete follows.
Concurrent independent searchIds do not share counters or cancellation state. Stale renderer generations cannot overwrite results or running state; cancellation in one session cannot finish another.

All tested normal/error/cancellation paths remove the completed worker's registry entry and wait for or terminate only its owned rg child. Tests do not mutate process-global PATH to simulate executable failure.

Existing matching/options, .gitignore, root authorization, bounds, rg/fallback selection, cancellation and renderer regression tests continue to pass without weakening assertions or budgets. Wire compatibility is checked with the actual existing consumer.

Graph ownership, file-local contracts, module maps and verification entries describe the final implementation. Exact-candidate final commands, hosted checks, review, lifecycle approval and collecting-lane bookkeeping are complete before delivery is called integrated. Required native/manual evidence is obtained or remains explicitly open under a separately granted exception.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Complete production-coordinator traces for both engines, all named success/error/cancellation cases, cross-session isolation, sequence ordering and zero post-terminal events; failing-first proof must detect the present embedded multi-root failure in the current tree.

Source-bound actual-consumer replay and supported-host/build-feature checks distinguish controlled diagnostics from native IPC. Preserve the existing eight-case backend and frontend receipts as historical reproduction rather than relabeling them as post-fix evidence.

One-root/multi-root embedded and rg native acceptance with synthetic authorized roots, results from both roots, cancellation and cleanup; unavailable platform/owner evidence remains open and is not substituted by a shim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The session-owner approach is an agent proposal supported by the existing single-terminal consumer contract; this draft does not record owner approval.

Later planning revalidates source hashes, active changes and the real lane baseline, including the diverged search-input-composition worktree. The already selected sequential mode is retained. Approval of this specification alone does not approve an unwritten plan, apply/archive, lane departure or release.
